page: Microsoft Azure F16-8amds_v7 is a compute and memory-oriented virtual machine configuration powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processors running at clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz. The instance provisions 8 dedicated physical cores with a 1:1 core-to-thread allocation on the x86_64 architecture. Cache configuration includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, backed by instruction extensions including AVX-512 (supporting VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic acceleration flags such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

A key characteristic of this configuration is its high memory-to-core density. Equipped with 128.0 GB of system RAM, it provides 16.0 GB per vCPU, diverging significantly from typical compute-focused memory ratios. For high-speed temporary disk access, the instance integrates 1890 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. The machine does not include discrete GPU accelerators and operates on the Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization hypervisor.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-core computational execution. Single-core tests in stress-ng reached 3730.67, landing in the top 10% tier. Single-threaded data handling was similarly fast, achieving 40.74 GB/sec in gzip compression and 18.08 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. Small-model LLM generation (135M parameters) hit 369.42 tokens per second. Multi-core operations align with standard 8-core expectations, recording 29555.44 on stress-ng multi-core and 24491.61 on PassMark CPU score.

Tradeoffs center around thread count and scaling capabilities. The 8 dedicated threads provide consistent per-thread performance and prevent noisy-neighbor contention, but multi-threaded parallel throughput is bounded relative to full-socket implementations. Memory bandwidth scales to 55.12 GB/sec for uncached reads and 34.25 GB/sec for uncached writes. Workloads that benefit from this balance include memory-intensive caching systems, in-memory databases, real-time data compression, single-threaded high-clock batch jobs, and analytics pipelines needing substantial RAM and fast local scratch storage.
description: Microsoft Azure F16-8amds_v7 is a virtual machine featuring 8 dedicated physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Built on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance combines dedicated CPU allocation with a substantial 128.0 GB of memory (16.0 GB per vCPU) and a bundled 1890 GB local NVMe SSD. It features modern instruction support including AVX-512 BF16 and VNNI, but does not include GPU acceleration. In benchmark assessments, the instance achieves top-tier single-core performance, delivering 3730.67 in stress-ng single-core tests alongside high-speed compression throughput of 40.74 GB/sec in gzip. Multi-core metrics remain average for an 8-thread setup, with a 24491.61 PassMark CPU score and 24.06 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. This server is structured for memory-heavy single-threaded tasks, in-memory databases, and high-speed data processing requiring fast local scratch storage.
